title: I, want
parentNote: Two words we just learn today, and the first is the biggest one in the course so far. Every story up to now has been about somebody else — Pete, Meg, Mark — because there was no way to spell the word a child most wants to say. I is one letter, it says its own name, it is always a capital, and no rule anywhere explains any of that, so it is simply remembered. want is here for a different reason: the w shoves the a sideways into an o, so a child sounding it out gets something that rhymes with ant. Don't let them battle it — say "the w is pushing that a about" and move on. The payoff is large and immediate. From today your child can read sentences about themselves — I want a big cake, I can see a bird — and that is what reading was for all along.

activities.sentence: I can see a big dog, and I want it.
activities.prompt: Do not sound this one out. One letter, standing on its own, and it says its own name: I.
The shortest word there is. It always gets a capital, even in the middle of a sentence. Say it: I.

activities.sentence: I want a red cake for supper.
activities.prompt: This one we just know too. The w bends the a, so do not sound it out: want.
No sounding out. Look at it and say it: want.
The word I says the same sound as this one, but with no e and nothing else at all.
And this is what an i usually says when it is stuck in the middle of a word. The word I refuses to do it.
Three jobs an a can do. In want it does none of them, and that is why we just learn it.
No new sound today, so these are all words you can already sound out.
The longest one. Six sounds, and the bossy r is right at the end.
All three start with w. Listen to the middle.
Two of these have a quiet e on the end. The vowel tells you which.

activities.text: I want a big red cake for supper!
I can see three ducks on the pond.
They want the cart, but I want the bike.
I did hunt for the lost card, and then I did spot it under the bed.

activities.title: The dog I want
activities.prompt: This story is the first one you get to tell about yourself. Read it one line at a time.
lines: I want a dog. I want a big dog with soft fur.
But Mum did tell Dad that a dog is hard.
I did ask and ask. Mum did just grin.
Then, in March, Dad came home with a crate.
The crate did shift, and then the crate did purr.
In the crate is a cat!
I did not want a cat. I want a dog.
The cat did jump up and did curl up on the bed.
The cat is soft, and it did purr and purr.
I still want a dog. But I want this cat, and I want it a lot!

questions.prompt: I want a big dog with ...
At the end I still want a dog, but I want the cat ...
